parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the clean-room reverse-engineering task: write a new original executable based on observed behavior of the provided binary and bundled docs only.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: It chose a six-child swarm for behavioral exploration, with every child assigned a specific research area and a note-file deliverable. No child was assigned implementation, integration, build, or final submission ownership.
parallel.implementation: The children ran extensive probes and produced research notes for CLI, control files, TLF/zip, and charset handling, while fontfile and layout research remained unfinished. No replacement source implementation was produced.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final packed artifact contained notes, fonts, tests, docs, and original workspace material, but no compiled replacement executable or compile script from an implementation effort.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification was limited to child black-box probes of the original binary; there was no integrated candidate implementation to build or compare before closure.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out after parent cancellation with four completed notes and two aborted research children, leaving the required implementation and build stage absent.

serial.requirements: The serial main agent recognized the same clean-room FIGlet reimplementation requirement and the constraints against internet/source reuse or wrapping the provided binary.
serial.plan_and_ownership: It kept a monolithic plan with probing first, then main-agent tasks for writing the C implementation, building a diff-test harness, fixing discrepancies, and writing compile.sh.
serial.implementation: It created helper/probe files in scratch and conducted many black-box experiments, but cancellation occurred before it wrote the implementation or build script.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact contained scratch probes and workspace materials, but no completed replacement source tree, executable build, or compile.sh deliverable.
serial.verification: Serial had planned a diff-test harness and final verification, but those tasks stayed pending and no integrated candidate reached official-aligned testing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out in the main trajectory during probing, so it also failed compile with no official tests run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent saw that the required deliverable was a new original executable matching the binary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent saw the same requirement and clean-room restrictions from the identical prompt.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements difference is visible; both understood the high-level reimplementation obligation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposition split six behavioral research topics into children, each with a note-file deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept implementation, harness, fixing, and compile.sh as main-agent todo items after probing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel made implementation unowned after delegation; serial retained it as the main agent's pending work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs contained rich probing scopes but no cross-agent implementation contract or final code handoff because no implementation components were assigned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no inter-agent context boundary; the same main context accumulated probing facts for eventual implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important boundary was ownership rather than a lossy or conflicting handoff: parallel had research briefs, serial had a single continuing context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced notes for four topics and left two research topics aborted, with no replacement code path started.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial directly probed behavior and generated scratch helpers, but implementation remained pending when cancellation arrived.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both omitted the implementation, but parallel omitted it through research-only delegation while serial simply never reached its own pending implementation stage.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received an aggregate swarm result with four completed children and two aborted children at cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; the main trajectory was cancelled while continuing its own probing work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure involved an incomplete swarm join, whereas serial closure was a single-agent cancellation without missing child joins.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel artifacts show note files as produced outputs; there is no implementation integration or final build placement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial artifacts show scratch experiments and helper files, but likewise no final implemented executable or compile script.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shared output was research notes rather than integrated source; serial's shared output was scratch evidence from one owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The completed official evaluation failed compilation and ran zero tests because no buildable solution was available.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The completed official evaluation also failed compilation and ran zero tests for the serial artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no outcome difference at the evaluator; both artifacts failed before tests could execute.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after a swarm wait and parent cancellation, with two child research scopes still aborted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial timed out in the main trajectory while probing, before pending implementation and build steps.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exhausted the run budget, but parallel spent closure budget in a research swarm while serial spent it in a single probing path.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial failed with compile_failed and 1044 tests not run. The useful comparison is that parallel converted the work into research-only child notes without an implementation owner, while serial retained implementation as pending main-agent work but timed out before executing it.
parallel_contributors: Research-only swarm delegation omitted an active owner for the required implementation and build deliverable.
Parent cancellation occurred after four note results and two aborted research children, before any implementation takeover.
serial_contributors: Single-agent probing consumed the run budget before the pending implementation and compile.sh tasks began.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Neither trajectory produced a code implementation, so no ordinary coding defect can be compared between submitted programs.

candidates.reason: The actual parallel work split assigned all six children to research/probing notes and left no active owner for producing the replacement implementation.
candidates.realized_consequence: No replacement implementation or build deliverable was present in the parallel artifact, leading to compile_failed with all tests not run.
candidates.near_match_reason: The research phase did not merely squeeze a later implementation phase; the delegated parallel plan never assigned an implementation owner.

Although investigators ran in parallel, the retained boundary is stronger: no active implementer existed after delegation, not just a completed investigation phase before late implementation.
The indispensable implementation path was not underallocated to a worker; it was unassigned, so Missing Owner is the direct boundary.
Six research children and timeout are visible, but the concrete adverse event is the research-only ownership plan, not excessive breadth alone.
Two research children were aborted, but no single child owned an overbroad implementation task whose unfinished output caused a separate consequence.
The children were briefed for research scopes; missing implementation in the child briefs reflects no implementation owner, not a child asked to implement with omitted requirements.
No separately owned implementation components were produced, so no incompatible cross-agent interface contract materialized.
There is no evidence that known task information was omitted or lost in transfer and then caused repeated or wrong downstream work.
Completed child note summaries were concise enough to return; the failure happened before implementation ownership, not because returned information was too large to consume.
No child result describes a superseded workspace or requirement state that the parent consumed incorrectly.
The returned research summaries do not present unresolved incompatible implementation contracts or conflicting reports at a decision point.
The parent never presented the whole task as complete or accepted a candidate solution before closure.
There was no replacement or retry child that restarted without inherited checkpoints and repeated prior work.
